content.text: All six preferred elements appear across §§ 13.1–13.3. No redline needed.

input.quote: 13.3 Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.
input.rationale: The licence package meets the preferred position in full. § 13.1 grants the subscription right to "Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf" (affiliates and contractors elements). § 13.2 grants a "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence" for paid-up software and Vendor Technology, including material embedded in a Deliverable (perpetual and irrevocable elements). § 13.3 limits Vendor revocation or suspension to a "material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure" (subscription licence terminable only for uncured material breach) and permits transfer to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by § 24, which § 24.1 confirms includes merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets without Vendor consent (successor transferability). "Affiliate" is defined in § 1.1 as a controlled/controlling/commonly controlled entity, so affiliate coverage is genuine and needs no written-notice fallback mechanic. The revocable, non-transferable Deliverable licence in § 14.2 is inconsistent in tone, but § 13.3's no-revocation rule and § 14.3's carry-through of the § 13.2 perpetual licence to Vendor Technology needed to use a Deliverable preserve our position; that Deliverable ownership/licence point is a Section 14 IP issue and we do not flag it twice here.
